pl-l4d24c10-d1e115.summary: States that the order of deacons holds the sixth place, because of the perfection of the number six.

pl-l4d24c10-d1e121.summary: Explains that in the Old Testament this order took its name from the tribe of Levi, consecrated after Aaron's ordination to divine worship, to serve before Aaron in the tabernacle, carry the ark and vessels, guard and move the tabernacle, from age twenty-five, a rule the Fathers kept in the New Testament since that age is strong for burdens. In Greek they are deacons, in Latin ministers, since as consecration belongs to the priest, the dispensing of ministry belongs to the deacon.
claims: Deacons dispense ministry as priests consecrate.

pl-l4d24c10-d1e130.summary: States that the deacon assists priests and ministers in all done in Christ's sacraments, baptism, chrism, paten and chalice, brings and arranges offerings, prepares and vests the Lord's table, carries the cross, and preaches the Gospel and Apostle; as lectors proclaim the Old Testament, deacons proclaim the New. He leads the prayers, reads the names of catechumens, bids attention to God, gives and announces the peace.
claims: Deacons assist in all sacraments and proclaim the Gospel.

pl-l4d24c10-d1e137.summary: Explains that what Moses established for this order is represented when the stole is placed on the deacon's left shoulder and the chasuble folded on fast days: whatever labor and endurance this life brings is borne on the left until rest is found on the right, in eternity.
claims: The stole on the left shoulder signifies bearing labor in this life.

pl-l4d24c10-d1e140.summary: States that the apostles established this order, choosing seven men full of the Holy Spirit and laying hands on them after prayer; hence the custom of seven deacons standing around Christ's altar in every mother church like seven columns, the seven angels with trumpets in the Apocalypse; Paul teaches Timothy what they should be.
claims: Seven deacons serve in every cathedral church.

pl-l4d24c10-d1e149.summary: States that at their ordination the bishop alone lays hands on them, since they are applied to ministry; he places the stole on the left shoulder, signifying the Lord's sweet yoke, and gives the Gospel book, showing they are heralds of Christ's Gospel; they should first be tested, as Paul teaches, and serve without crime.
claims: Only the bishop lays hands on deacons.
Deacons receive stole and Gospel book.
Deacons must be tested and blameless.

pl-l4d24c10-d1e161.summary: States that Christ used this office when after the Supper he distributed the sacrament of his flesh and blood to the disciples, and when he roused the sleeping apostles to prayer: watch and pray, lest you enter into temptation.

pl-l4d24c10.summary: The deacons hold the sixth place, for the perfection of the number six. The order took its name from the tribe of Levi, consecrated to serve in the tabernacle from age twenty-five; deacons, 'ministers', have the dispensing of ministry as the priest has consecration. They assist priests in all the sacraments, bring offerings, prepare the Lord's table, carry the cross, preach the Gospel, lead prayers, and announce the peace. The stole on the left shoulder signifies bearing labor in this life. The apostles established the order by choosing seven men; the bishop alone lays hands on them, gives the stole and the Gospel book; they must be tested and blameless. Christ used this office in giving the sacrament to the disciples and in urging them to watch and pray.
claims: Deacons assist priests in all the sacraments and preach the Gospel.
The order derives from the Levites and was established by the apostles.
Only the bishop lays hands on deacons.
Deacons must be tested and blameless.
Christ exercised this office at the Supper.
